# Pose-free and Feed-forward Training

Also called: Pose-free Gaussian Splatting, Feed-forward 3DGS, Generalizable 3DGS

## Overview
This family enables 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction without iterative per-scene optimization or known camera poses. It solves the dependency on Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipelines and slow differentiable rendering loops by using neural networks to directly predict Gaussian primitives from images [S1, unofficial]. Unlike standard [3D Gaussian Splatting Training](3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md) which requires known poses and iterative gradient descent, these methods are either feed-forward (instant inference) or use fixed priors to bypass pose learning [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism replaces the iterative optimization loop of standard 3DGS with a direct mapping from image space to Gaussian parameter space, or fixes poses via external priors.

1.  **Input:** Uncalibrated images $\{I_i\}$ (intrinsics and extrinsics unknown or ignored) [S1, unofficial].
2.  **Output:** A set of 3D Gaussian primitives $\{G_i\}$ defined by mean $\mu_i$, covariance $\Sigma_i$, opacity $\alpha_i$, and spherical harmonics coefficients $c_{i,lm}$ [6136-instantsplat.md][6464-pixelsplat.md].
3.  **Differentiability:** The rendering process is differentiable with respect to the scene representation. In feed-forward methods, gradients flow through the network weights; in prior-based methods, gradients update the Gaussian attributes while poses remain fixed [S1, 6136-instantsplat.md, 6464-pixelsplat.md, unofficial].
4.  **Loss Function:** Minimization of photometric reconstruction error:
    $$ \mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{L1} + \lambda \mathcal{L}_{MS-SSIM} $$
    or
    $$ \mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{MSE} + \lambda \mathcal{L}_{LPIPS} $$
    [6136-instantsplat.md][6464-pixelsplat.md].

## Subtopics

### [InstantSplat](6136-instantsplat.md)
InstantSplat is a pose-free, sparse-view method that reconstructs scenes from uncalibrated images in seconds by leveraging MASt3R or VGGT geometry priors. It distinguishes itself from feed-forward methods like [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md) by relying on geometry priors for initialization rather than direct image-to-Gaussian regression, and from joint pose optimization by fixing poses via priors rather than learning them[6464-pixelsplat.md].

### [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md)
pixelSplat is a feed-forward model that reconstructs a 3D radiance field parameterized by 3D Gaussian primitives from a pair of input images. It solves the problem of generalizable novel view synthesis by producing an explicit, editable 3D representation that renders in real-time, avoiding the memory and time intensity of ray-marching based methods. Unlike light-field transformers which output implicit fields, pixelSplat generates a primitive-based structure that is significantly faster to encode and render. It specifically addresses two key challenges in sparse-view reconstruction: scale ambiguity inherent in Structure-from-Motion (SfM) poses and local minima in primitive regression, using an epipolar transformer and differentiable probabilistic sampling respectively.

### [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md)
Joint Pose Optimization refers to methods that simultaneously optimize camera poses and the underlying 3D radiance field representation, eliminating the strict dependency on external Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipelines for initial pose estimation. Unlike standard differentiable rendering which assumes known camera parameters, this approach treats poses as learnable variables optimized via photometric loss. It is distinguished from sibling methods like [InstantSplat](6136-instantsplat.md) and [pixelSplat](6464-pixelsplat.md) by its reliance on iterative gradient-based optimization of pose parameters rather than direct feed-forward regression or pre-computed depth priors.

#### AnySplat
Pose-free feed-forward network: a single forward pass over uncalibrated image collections yields 3D Gaussian primitives plus per-image intrinsics and extrinsics [S1, unofficial]. It scales to casual dense or sparse multi-view captures with no pose annotations, matching pose-aware baselines and surpassing prior pose-free methods (NoPoSplat-class) in zero-shot evaluations at real-time rendering latency [S1, unofficial].

## Background
Originating from the need to accelerate 3D Gaussian Splatting training and remove SfM dependencies, this family emerged alongside generalizable view synthesis methods like MVSplat and latentSplat [S1, unofficial]. Key developments include InstantSplat (sparse-view, prior-based) and pixelSplat (feed-forward, 2-view) [S1, unofficial]. Recent variants like AnySplat extend this to uncalibrated multi-view collections [S1, unofficial].
